# Function reference

<!-- generated by scripts/gen_docs.py - do not edit -->

All functions take file **paths**; `out` is always optional (a new `<name>_<what>.pdf` is created next to the source, never overwriting; `inplace=True` overwrites). Pages, lines and image numbers are **1-based**. They return a `Result` (`r.out` = file or folder written).

## Shrink / combine / split

### `compress`

```python
pypdfcraft.compress(src, out=None, *, preset=None, inplace=False, password=None, keep_original=True, **options)
```

Make the PDF smaller -> ``<name>_compressed.pdf`` (or ``out``).

No options = Acrobat-style "Reduce File Size".  ``preset="mobile"`` or options such as
``discard_thumbnails=True`` use the PDF Optimizer.  If the file can't get smaller the engine
writes nothing; with ``keep_original=True`` the output is then a copy and ``r.written`` is False.

### `merge`

```python
pypdfcraft.merge(paths, out=None, *, pages=None, passwords=None, field_conflicts=None)
```

Combine files in order -> ``<first>_merged.pdf`` (or ``out``).  Images, .txt, .docx/.xlsx/.pptx/.rtf also work.
``pages``: per-file ranges like ``["1-3, 6", None]``; ``passwords``: per file.

### `split`

```python
pypdfcraft.split(src, out_dir=None, *, every=None, before=None, bookmarks=None, max_mb=None, password=None)
```

Split into ``<name>-partK.pdf`` files in ``<name>_parts/`` (or ``out_dir``).
Give exactly one criterion: every=N pages, before=[pages], bookmarks=True, max_mb=N.

### `extract_pages`

```python
pypdfcraft.extract_pages(src, pages, out=None, *, password=None)
```

Copy the given 1-based pages into a new PDF -> ``<name>_pages.pdf``.

### `delete_pages`

```python
pypdfcraft.delete_pages(src, pages, *, out=None, inplace=False, password=None)
```

Remove the given 1-based pages -> ``<name>_edited.pdf``.

### `move_pages`

```python
pypdfcraft.move_pages(src, pages, to, *, out=None, inplace=False, password=None)
```

Move pages so they start at position ``to``.

### `reverse_pages`

```python
pypdfcraft.reverse_pages(src, pages=None, *, out=None, inplace=False, password=None)
```

Reverse the page order (or of the given pages) -> ``<name>_reversed.pdf``.

### `rotate`

```python
pypdfcraft.rotate(src, degrees, pages=None, *, out=None, inplace=False, password=None, **options)
```

Rotate by a multiple of 90 (positive = clockwise); ``pages`` default: all.

## Edit text (real PDF text)

### `show_lines`

```python
pypdfcraft.show_lines(src, page=None, password=None)
```

Print the numbered lines so you can choose one: ``p1 #3  [Helvetica 12pt]  Hello world``.

### `lines`

```python
pypdfcraft.lines(src, page=None, password=None)
```

Numbered text lines ``[{page, line, text, rect, font, size}]`` (all pages if ``page`` is None).

### `paragraphs`

```python
pypdfcraft.paragraphs(src, page=None, password=None)
```

Numbered paragraphs ``[{page, paragraph, text, rect, font, size, bold, italic, color}]``.

### `find`

```python
pypdfcraft.find(src, query, password=None)
```

Where ``query`` occurs (page + rectangles).

### `replace_text`

```python
pypdfcraft.replace_text(src, old, new, *, out=None, pages=None, case_sensitive=False, first_only=False, mode='auto', inplace=False, missing_ok=False, password=None)
```

Replace a phrase in the real text of the PDF (like editing a line in the app).

    replace_text("contract.pdf", "2023", "2024")           # -> contract_edited.pdf
    replace_text("a.pdf", "Mr. Smith", "Ms. Jones", inplace=True)

``mode``: 'line' (default behaviour of 'auto') edits single lines; use 'paragraph' for phrases that
wrap across lines.  Raises TextNotFound when nothing matched (``missing_ok=True`` to ignore).

### `edit_line`

```python
pypdfcraft.edit_line(src, page, line, text, *, out=None, inplace=False, password=None, **style)
```

Replace line number ``line`` (see ``show_lines``) on ``page`` with ``text``.

### `edit_paragraph`

```python
pypdfcraft.edit_paragraph(src, page, paragraph, text=None, *, out=None, inplace=False, password=None, **format)
```

Edit/restyle a paragraph (``paragraphs(src, page)`` shows numbers).
``format``: font, bold, italic, size, color, align, line_spacing, dx, dy, width ...

### `interactive_edit`

```python
pypdfcraft.interactive_edit(src, out=None, *, inplace=False, password=None)
```

Console editor: pick a page, pick a line number, type the new text.  ``q`` saves, ``x`` discards.

### `add_text`

```python
pypdfcraft.add_text(src, page, text, *, at=None, rect=None, out=None, inplace=False, password=None, **style)
```

Put new text on a page at ``at=[x, y]`` points from the top-left (style: font, size, bold, color ...).


Convert in either direction.  The source type is detected from its extension.

convert("report.pdf", "docx")      # PDF -> Word      (xlsx, pptx, html, md, txt)
convert("report.pdf", "png")       # PDF -> pictures  (jpg, tiff) in a folder, one per page
convert("report.pdf", "pdfa")      # PDF -> PDF/A
convert("letter.docx")             # Word/Excel/PowerPoint/RTF -> PDF
convert("photo.jpg")               # picture -> PDF        (use merge()/images_to_pdf for many)

## Any tool

### `apply`

```python
pypdfcraft.apply(src, tool, /, *, out=None, inplace=False, password=None, suffix='edited', **args)
```

Run **any** engine tool on a file in one call (all 186 are reachable this way).

    apply("a.pdf", "doc_flatten", fields=True)           # modifies -> saved to a_edited.pdf
    apply("a.pdf", "text_word_count")                    # read-only -> nothing is written
    apply("a.pdf", "page_rotate", degrees=90, out="r.pdf")

The file is opened, ``tool`` is run with ``args``, and - only if the tool changed the document -
the result is saved to ``out`` (default ``<name>_<suffix>.pdf``; ``inplace=True`` overwrites).
Tools that write their own files (exports, splits ...) leave the document untouched, so nothing
extra is saved.  Returns a :class:`Result`; ``r.out`` is the saved file (if any).
See ``pypdfcraft.search("...")`` / ``TOOLS.md`` for tool names and their arguments.

### `run_tool`

```python
pypdfcraft.run_tool(tool, /, **args)
```

Run an engine tool that does not work on one open document (``doc_combine``, ``sign_id_create``,
``doc_bates_multi``, ``printers`` ...).  Returns a :class:`Result`.

## Read aloud

### `read_aloud`

```python
pypdfcraft.read_aloud(src, pages=None, *, voice=None, language=None, rate=1.0, volume=1.0, backend=None, password=None, on_paragraph=None, on_word=None, wait=True)
```

Speak the PDF's text in reading order with the system voice (see the module docs for the engines).

    read_aloud("book.pdf")                       # everything
    read_aloud("book.pdf", pages=[3, 4], rate=1.3, voice="en-us")

Returns the :class:`ReadAloud` controller (``stop()``, ``pause()``, ``forward()`` ...); with ``wait=False`` it
keeps reading in the background.  Raises :class:`NoSpeechEngine` if the machine has no speech engine and
``PdfCraftError`` if there is no text (scanned pages: run ``ocr()`` first).

### `to_audio`

```python
pypdfcraft.to_audio(src, out=None, pages=None, *, voice=None, language=None, rate=1.0, volume=1.0, backend=None, password=None)
```

Write the spoken text to an audio file -> ``<name>.wav`` (engines: espeak-ng, macOS say, Windows SAPI, pyttsx3).

### `reading_text`

```python
pypdfcraft.reading_text(src, pages=None, *, password=None)
```

The paragraphs Read Aloud would speak: ``[{page, index, text}]`` in reading order.

### `voices`

```python
pypdfcraft.voices(backend=None)
```

Voices the speech engine offers (names usable as ``voice=``).

### `ReadAloud`

```python
pypdfcraft.ReadAloud(source, *, pages=None, start_page=None, voice=None, language=None, rate=1.0, volume=1.0, backend=None, password=None, max_chars=1500, on_paragraph=None, on_word=None)
```

Speak a document paragraph by paragraph, like PdfCraft's Android Read Aloud.

``source``: a path or an open :class:`~pypdfcraft.Document`.  ``pages``: 1-based list/range (default all).
``rate`` 1.0 = normal speed.  ``on_paragraph(p)`` is called when a paragraph starts and ``on_word(w)`` for every
word (``w.rect`` = ``[x0, y0, x1, y1]`` in PDF points from the top-left, ``w.page``, ``w.text``, ``w.paragraph``);
word callbacks are exact with the ``pyttsx3`` engine and timed estimates otherwise.

    r = ReadAloud("a.pdf", pages=range(1, 4), rate=1.1)
    r.play()                          # blocks;  r.play(wait=False) returns at once
    r.stop(); r.pause(); r.resume(); r.forward(); r.back()
